clue.text: Startle fan of Cockneys?

parts.note: Bow, in East London, is the home of the Cockney, born within the sound of Bow bells
a fan is a lover or devotee of something

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about who it is that admires London's Cockneys.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'fan of Cockneys' is a BOW LOVER: Bow is the East London district whose church bells define a true Cockney.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bowled over is to be astonished, so the phrasal verb means to surprise greatly.

clue.text: Musical drama's a long time in the eye

definitions.note: possessive phrase meaning belonging to opera, an adjective like the answer

indicators.note: the long time sits inside the word for the eye, as the clue's 'in' says

parts.note: optic is a word for the eye
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A remark that an opera seems to take forever to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective describing things that belong to opera, the dramatic form sung to music.

clue.text: Form of dancing requiring nothing on leg, say

parts.note: a leg is an example of a limb
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A dance that needs you to wear nothing on your legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the leg as just one example of a LIMB; O for nothing goes on after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is a Caribbean dance in which performers lean back to pass under a lowered bar.

clue.text: The quickest-selling cosmetic?

parts.note: a product that sells so fast it disappears from the shelves, read as a cosmetic named for disappearing

explanation.surface: A question about which beauty product flies off the shelves fastest.
explanation.walkthrough: Goods that sell fast are said to vanish; the cream named for vanishing is a real cosmetic that soaks invisibly into the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a light skin cream that leaves no visible film once rubbed in.

clue.text: Some Pictish tribe recently turning up in fresh appearance

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the run is read from bottom to top, backwards
only some of the letters in the words that follow are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A Pictish tribe has recently reappeared in a new form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes HTRIBER from 'PictisH TRIBE Recently'; 'turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebirth is a new emergence or revival, a coming back into view afresh.

clue.text: Hard and well-established wrestling manoeuvre

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
something well-established is old

explanation.surface: A tough, long-practised grappling move in a wrestling bout.
explanation.definitionFit: In wrestling a hold is a grip used to pin or control an opponent.

clue.text: Variant of this early locksmith's work?

indicators.note: a variant is a changed version, so these letters are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A rough version of something a primitive locksmith made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variant of' rearranges THIS EARLY. The 'locksmith' is someone who works on locks of hair, not door locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks are tresses of hair, so a smith working on them produces a hairdo.

clue.text: Army, say, captured by brave man

indicators.note: the short piece is held inside the brave man, as a captive is held

parts.note: a lion is a brave person
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A soldier captured by some brave fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a Roman army unit, and the word still means a large host of troops.

clue.text: Fruit of pugilism? Yes and no

definitions.text: Fruit of pugilism? Yes and no

parts.words: Fruit of pugilism? Yes and no
parts.note: the result of boxing that is named after a vegetable, so a fruit and not a fruit

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a boxing career yields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit' means result, and the injury is named after a vegetable, which is a kind of produce but not a fruit, hence 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated blows swell a boxer's ear into a lumpy shape like the vegetable's head.

clue.text: Article on source of disease from part of Europe

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a germ is a microbe that causes illness
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about where an illness started in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something that comes from Germany, a central European country.

clue.text: Complaining, getting left out in defeat

indicators.note: out signals that the letter for left is dropped

parts.note: bleating means whining or complaining

explanation.surface: Someone whining about being left out after losing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting left out' drops the L from BLEATING.
explanation.definitionFit: A beating is a heavy loss, as when a team is thrashed.

clue.text: Drinker-driver getting in round?

indicators.note: the round letter goes inside the driver phrase

parts.note: a driver is someone who uses a car, a car user
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A drink-driver joining in to buy a round at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins definition and wordplay: 'Drinker' defines, 'driver' gives CAR USER, and O goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser is someone who drinks heavily and noisily in company.

clue.text: Rumour reflecting on Liberal causes damage

indicators.note: reflecting means mirrored, so the word for rumour reads backwards

parts.note: noise can mean rumour or talk, as in noises about something

explanation.surface: Gossip about a Liberal politician does harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' reverses NOISE to ESION, which follows L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is an injury or wound to body tissue, physical harm.

clue.text: Porcine power taking on insect? I don't believe it! 2

parts.note: porcine means of pigs, standing for the animals themselves
might means power or strength
a fly is an insect

explanation.surface: A pig's strength being turned on a bug, which nobody would credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '2' is a printing mark, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses disbelief: something will happen only when farm animals take to the air.

clue.text: Academist reviewed photographer's aid

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looking at again in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A member of the academy reviewing equipment for a cameraman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Steadicam is a body-mounted stabiliser that keeps a moving camera steady.

clue.text: Appearing in double Dutch style?

parts.note: Dutch is slang for wife, so double Dutch means having two wives

explanation.surface: Something that seems like gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double Dutch' looks like gibberish, but 'Dutch' is old Cockney slang for a wife (from duchess), so double Dutch is two wives.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigamous person has married a second spouse while still married to the first.

clue.text: Double first in English 3 and one drink after receiving university info 4 covering epic poetry

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before, the later ones after
the two copies of the letter take in the next pieces between them
double means the letter appears twice
only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: gen is slang for information
taken as written
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: An instruction for a scholar celebrating a double first with drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of English, doubled, receives U and GEN to make EUGENE; ONE and GIN follow. The '3' and '4' are printing marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushkin's novel in verse is a long narrative poem, a celebrated work of Russian poetry.

clue.text: Girl with English blokes will be upset — that's Fate

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a girl
blokes are men

explanation.surface: A girl and some English men will be upset, and that is destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: SIS + E + MEN is reversed by 'will be upset'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is the Greek goddess of retribution, and the word means an inescapable doom.

clue.text: Method of propelling barge on stream

parts.note: to barge into is to ram
a jet is a stream of fluid

explanation.surface: A way of pushing a canal barge along a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramjet is an engine that compresses air by forward speed alone to drive an aircraft.

clue.text: Norse hero not so much covered

definitions.meaning: The Norse god of light, slain by mistletoe
comparative of bald, having less hair or covering

explanation.surface: A Viking warrior who is less well covered.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the beloved Norse god, son of Odin; the other is the comparative adjective of hairless.

clue.text: Rich man showing sense: 'Best backing ousting king'

indicators.note: backing means the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: someone sane shows good sense

indicators.note: ousting means the king's letter is thrown out

parts.note: the cream is the best of anything
R is the abbreviation for king, from rex

explanation.surface: A wealthy man sensibly backing the best, though not the king.
explanation.walkthrough: CREAM loses R ('ousting king') to CEAM; SANE + CEAM is reversed by 'backing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maecenas was a wealthy Roman patron of poets, and his name stands for any rich patron.

clue.text: Someone in club heading off remnant

indicators.note: the first letter is removed from the front

parts.note: a member belongs to a club

explanation.surface: A club member leaving, the last of the gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the first letter of MEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing fragment left from a fire, a leftover piece.

clue.text: Sailor leading a ship is a fool

indicators.note: the sailor goes before the rest

parts.note: jack is a word for a sailor
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A sailor commanding a vessel is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackass is a male donkey, and figuratively a stupid person.

clue.text: Ultimate in style, note, getting hair cut in a single mass

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: NB, nota bene, means take note

indicators.note: the hair word loses its last letter, as if trimmed

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: A stylish note about a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'style' (E), then NB for note, then LOCK cut short to LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: French phrase meaning all together as a group, one body.

clue.text: A small thing, neglecting half the letters

definitions.meaning: a tiny particle, the smallest unit of matter
running from A to M covers only the first half of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A minor matter that skips half the letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'A to M', the word covers the first half of the alphabet and leaves out N to Z.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the tiniest particle of an element; the other reads the word as 'A to M', the first thirteen letters only.

clue.text: Haydn symphony almost certain to get radio-based award

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: on the radio, a word is only heard, so it sounds the same as another

parts.note: a prize is an award

explanation.surface: A Haydn work almost guaranteed to win a radio prize.
explanation.walkthrough: SURE loses its last letter ('almost'); PRISE sounds like PRIZE, as 'radio-based' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's Symphony No. 94 is nicknamed for its sudden loud chord in the slow movement.
